_readme: Labeled classification cases for evals/classify.mjs — the ACCURACY eval (did Cherry classify correctly?), as opposed to check.mjs, the CONTRACT eval (is the output well-formed?). Each case is a short paste-mode feedback bundle with ONE dominant issue, so the top-ranked issue is the one being graded. 'expect.owner' is a list because routing can have more than one defensible answer; disposition and signalType are exact-match. Boundary cases are deliberate — they sit on the line the prompt has to hold (surface fix vs capability signal is the blurry one). Grow this file from production misses: every classification a human corrects becomes a candidate case.

cases.note: clear bug — the easy anchor case
cases.feedback:
Ticket #4411: App crashes every time I export a project over 200MB. Reproduced on two machines.
Ticket #4415: Export to PDF just dies with a spinner, file never downloads. Started after the last update.
Ticket #4420: Same crash on export here. Losing work because of it.

cases.note: deliberate business choice — must NOT be framed as a fix-it ticket
cases.feedback:
Trustpilot-style paste: 'Cancelling took me 45 minutes, four confirmation screens, and a mandatory retention call. This is designed to stop you leaving.'
Support thread: 'Customer furious about the $180 early termination fee — says it was buried in the signup flow.'
Another: 'The cancel button is hidden behind three menus on purpose. Predatory.'

cases.note: AI product, core capability failing across a use case — the capability-signal anchor
cases.feedback:
User interview notes: 'The meeting transcription consistently mishears our Indian and Scottish colleagues — names, numbers, all garbled. We can't share notes without a full manual pass.'
Support ticket: 'Transcripts are unusable for our Singapore office. Accuracy is fine for US accents only.'
Sales call note: prospect passed on the deal, said transcription quality on non-US accents was the blocker for a global team.

cases.note: boundary: reads like a feature complaint, is actually the core capability underperforming
cases.feedback:
Slack #feedback: 'The AI summary of our 90-minute planning doc missed both decisions we actually made and highlighted the small talk.'
'Same — summaries are fine for short docs but anything long, it loses the thread and I have to re-read the whole thing anyway.'
'Asked it to summarize the contract review; it skipped the liability clause entirely. That's the one thing I needed.'

cases.note: boundary the other way: mentions scale/limits but is a boundable bug, not a systemic gap
cases.feedback:
Ticket: 'Uploading a 1.2GB video fails at 99% every single time. Small files are fine.'
Ticket: 'Upload of large media files times out — progress bar hits the end then errors.'
Forum post: 'Known issue? Big uploads die at the last second. Retried five times.'

Support ticket: 'I was charged twice this month, two identical invoices dated the same day.'
Support ticket: 'Duplicate charge on my card after the plan renewal, still no refund after 10 days.'
Chat log: 'Billed for 12 seats, we only have 8. Second month running.'

cases.note: an ops gap, not a product bug — owner is the support org
cases.feedback:
NPS verbatim: 'Took 9 days to get a first response on a P1 ticket. Unacceptable at this price.'
NPS verbatim: 'Support is a black hole. Auto-reply, then silence for a week.'
Renewal call note: CS flagged that the account nearly churned over response times, not the product itself.

cases.note: deliberate monetization choice customers hate — strategy call, not a ticket
cases.feedback:
App review: 'Every single session opens with a full-screen upgrade modal. I already pay for Plus!'
App review: 'Three upsell popups before I can do anything. It's relentless and clearly intentional.'
Reddit-style paste: 'They A/B tested even MORE upgrade nags last month. Product is good, the constant selling is why I'm leaving.'

cases.note: boundary: for a search-centric product, bad relevance is the core capability, not a UI bug
cases.feedback:
User research notes (product: an enterprise knowledge-search tool): 'Search returns documents that merely contain the words, not what I meant. For anything beyond exact keywords it's useless.'
'Asked for the Q3 pricing deck, got 40 results, the actual deck was #17.'
'Our team has reverted to asking each other in Slack because search can't find things by meaning. That's the whole reason we bought it.'

cases.note: content defect — routes to the docs/content owner, not core engineering
cases.feedback:
GitHub-style paste: 'The quickstart example in the docs throws a TypeError as written — the import path changed two versions ago and the docs never caught up.'
'Copy-pasted the webhook tutorial verbatim, three of the five snippets fail.'
'Docs code samples are consistently stale. New users bounce off the first tutorial.'

cases.note: revenue-carrying case — also exercises revenueContext extraction
cases.feedback:
Sales call notes: 'Acme Corp ($400K/yr renewal) says no SSO/SAML is now a hard compliance blocker — security team will not approve renewal without it.'
CS note: 'Two more mid-market accounts (~$60K combined) asked for SSO this quarter, same compliance driver.'
Opportunity-loss reason: 'Lost Initech deal at contract stage: no SSO.'
